instruction.text: Read the sentences and answer the questions.

atoms.text: 1. The coding language Python was invented in 1989 by Guido van Rossum.
atoms.sound: The coding language Python was invented in 1989 by Guido van Rossum.

atoms.text: 2. Learning how to code is becoming increasingly important and should be part of the curriculum in school.
atoms.sound: Learning how to code is becoming increasingly important and should be part of the curriculum in school.

atoms.text: 3. Why is coding not commonly taught in schools, even though it has become increasingly relevant for many jobs?
atoms.sound: Why is coding not commonly taught in schools, even though it has become increasingly relevant for many jobs?

atoms.a: Which sentence would be a good thesis statement?

trainers.instruction: Select the pieces of evidence that strengthen the argument.

atoms.a: Learning how to code is becoming increasingly important and should be part of the curriculum in school.
b: ++For example, coding is needed to build apps that millions of people use on a daily basis.
First Lady Helen Herron Taft was already dead when the programming language Python was created.
++Studies show that people who know how to code can find creative solutions to big problems more easily.
Children are naturally curious and will learn how to code by themselves.

atoms.b:
When you write a ((claim)) or an argument, you can think of the structure of this house. First, you should state your claim.
Then, you should give evidence that ((supports)) your claim.
Naming some facts and ((examples)) is a good way to give evidence for your argument.

A ((thesis_statement)) can be made up of several claims. Each claim must be supported by ((evidence)), facts and examples to make the argument ((convincing)).
You can think of multiple 'claim-houses' — as you see in the picture above — that ((support)) your thesis statement.
